title: African Centre for School Leadership Grants 2026: Apply for Up to $35,000 in School Leadership Research Funding
summary: The African Centre for School Leadership (ACSL) , in partnership with the Mastercard Foundation , has announced a new call for applications for its Cohort II School Leadership Research Grants , providing African education researchers with an opportunity to secure funding for action-oriented research focused on strengthening school leadership and improving learning outcomes across the continent. The 2026 ACSL grants will support researchers undertaking descriptive and comparative action research addressing critical challenges in school leadership across African education systems. A total of 23 researchers will be supported through the initiative, with individual grants worth up to US$15,000 for descriptive action research and up to US$35,000 for comparative action research . The programme is designed not only to fund research but also to ensure that research findings translate into practical improvements in schools, education policy and education systems. Successful researchers will have opportunities to work with policymakers, practitioners, school leaders and implementing institutions throughout their research journey. Applications are open to eligible researchers from all African countries , with proposals particularly encouraged to address issues such as gender equality, disability inclusion, rural and underserved communities, and other marginalised groups. Overview of the ACSL School Leadership Research Grants The African Centre for School Leadership is seeking researchers who are passionate about generating evidence that can strengthen school leadership practices and contribute to improved educational outcomes in Africa. The grants are intended to support rigorous, action-oriented research rather than research that remains solely academic. Applicants are expected to demonstrate how their research can contribute to solving real-world school leadership challenges and how relevant stakeholders will be involved in the research process. The initiative will support two different categories of research: Descriptive Action Research Grants Comparative Action Research Grants Together, these grants will provide funding for 23 researchers across Africa . 1. Descriptive Action Research Grants The ACSL will award 16 Descriptive Action Research Grants , with each grant providing funding of up to US$15,000 . These grants are designed for research conducted within one educational context over a period of 12 months . A descriptive action research project could, for example, examine school leadership practices, challenges, policies or interventions within a particular country, education system, region, district or other defined educational context. The research should ultimately generate evidence that can be used by education stakeholders to strengthen school leadership and improve educational outcomes. Key details Number of grants: 16 Maximum funding: US$15,000 per grant Research duration: 12 months Research scope: One educational context Research approach: Action research Geographic eligibility: African countries 2. Comparative Action Research Grants The second category consists of seven Comparative Action Research Grants . Each successful applicant/team can receive up to US$35,000 to conduct research across two or more educational contexts . These grants will run for a longer period of 24 months , allowing researchers to investigate school leadership issues comparatively across different settings. Comparative research can provide valuable insights into similarities and differences in school leadership practices, policies and outcomes across countries or other educational contexts. Key details Number of grants: 7 Maximum funding: US$35,000 per grant Research duration: 24 months Research scope: Two or more educational contexts Research approach: Comparative action research Geographic eligibility: African countries What Is the Main Purpose of the ACSL Research Grants? The ACSL School Leadership Research Grants are intended to address some of the challenges affecting school leadership across Africa while ensuring that research produces practical value for education systems. The programme seeks to support research that can: Generate evidence on school leadership challenges in Africa. Strengthen school leadership practices. Contribute to improved learning outcomes. Inform education policy. Support education practitioners and school leaders. Strengthen education systems. Encourage collaboration between researchers and practitioners. Connect research findings with policymakers. Promote evidence-based decision-making. Address challenges affecting underserved communities. Contribute to national and continental education priorities. Rather than separating researchers from the people who implement education policies and manage schools, the programme encourages meaningful engagement between researchers, policymakers, practitioners and school leaders. Research Must Use an Action-Research Approach One of the important requirements of the call is that proposals must adopt an action-research approach . Applicants should therefore ensure that their proposed research is designed to investigate real challenges while also contributing to practical improvements. The research should demonstrate meaningful collaboration with relevant stakeholders, particularly: Policymakers Education practitioners School leaders Implementing institutions Other relevant education stakeholders This approach is intended to ensure that research findings do not simply remain in academic publications but can contribute to improvements in policy and practice. Strong Encouragement for Inclusive Research The ACSL is particularly encouraging proposals that take into account issues affecting groups that may experience barriers or disadvantages within education systems. Proposals addressing the following areas are strongly encouraged: Gender equality Researchers can explore school leadership challenges and opportunities through a gender perspective, including issues affecting women s participation and leadership in education. Disability inclusion Research focusing on inclusive school leadership and education systems that better serve people with disabilities is also encouraged. Rural and underserved communities Applicants are encouraged to consider the realities of schools and communities that may have limited access to resources, leadership capacity or educational opportunities. Marginalised groups Research addressing the challenges faced by other marginalised populations is also encouraged under the programme. The call therefore presents an opportunity for researchers to develop studies that address both school leadership and broader equity and inclusion challenges in African education. Who Can Apply for the ACSL Grants? The opportunity is open to researchers who meet specific eligibility requirements. Applicants must satisfy the geographic, academic, research-team and methodological requirements established by the African Centre for School Leadership. 1. Applicants must be African citizens Applicants must be citizens of an African country . The applicant must also be based in Africa . The proposed research must focus on school leadership practice in one or multiple African countries . This means the programme is specifically designed to strengthen African-led research on African education systems. 2. The Principal Investigator must hold a doctorate A particularly important eligibility requirement concerns the Principal Investigator. The Principal Investigator must hold a Doctorate in one of the following areas: Education Educational Leadership Educational Management A closely related field The doctorate must have been earned within the past five years . Applicants should therefore carefully consider the date on which the Principal Investigator obtained their doctoral degree when determining eligibility. 3. Proposals must have multidisciplinary teams Applications cannot simply be built around a single researcher. Proposals must include multidisciplinary research teams consisting of three to five members . This requirement encourages applicants to bring together researchers with different areas of expertise and perspectives. A strong multidisciplinary team can potentially provide expertise across areas such as education, leadership, policy, research methodology, management, inclusion and other relevant fields. Diversity Within Research Teams The ACSL strongly encourages applicants to build diverse research teams. In particular, research teams are encouraged to include: Female researchers Young researchers under the age of 35 Researchers with different educational backgrounds Researchers holding bachelor s degrees Researchers holding master s degrees Doctoral researchers or candidates This emphasis on diversity is intended to broaden perspectives within research teams and provide opportunities for researchers at different stages of their academic and professional development. Cross-Country Collaboration Is Encouraged Applicants conducting research across multiple African countries are also encouraged to consider cross-country collaboration. This is particularly relevant to applicants interested in the Comparative Action Research Grants , which support research across two or more educational contexts. Cross-country research can provide opportunities to compare: School leadership models Education policies Leadership practices Institutional structures Challenges facing school leaders Approaches to improving learning outcomes Strategies for addressing educational inequality Researchers interested in comparative research should therefore consider how collaboration across different African education systems can strengthen the proposed study. What Happens Beyond the Grant Funding? The opportunity provides more than financial support. Successful researchers will become part of the School Leadership Community of Learning . They will also participate in the Blended Exchange and Learning Trajectory (BELT) . This means successful applicants will have an opportunity to engage with a broader community of researchers and education stakeholders working on school leadership issues. Participation in these activities can potentially help researchers: Exchange knowledge with other African researchers. Learn from different school leadership experiences. Share research findings. Build professional connections. Engage with education stakeholders. Strengthen the practical relevance of their research. Contribute to a wider evidence base on school leadership in Africa. The community element is therefore an important part of the programme beyond the direct research funding. Information Webinar for Prospective Applicants The African Centre for School Leadership will organise an information webinar for prospective applicants. The webinar is intended to provide guidance on important aspects of the application process, including: Application procedures Eligibility criteria Grant expectations Other relevant information for prospective applicants Webinar date and time Date: 20 August 2026 Time: 12:00–1:30 pm GMT East Africa Time: 3:00–4:30 pm EAT Prospective applicants are encouraged to participate in the webinar to gain a better understanding of the grant requirements before submitting their applications. Application Deadline Applicants must submit their applications before the stated deadline. Deadline: Wednesday, 30 September 2026 at 11:59 pm GMT. Researchers should avoid waiting until the final hours to submit their applications. Preparing a strong research proposal, assembling a multidisciplinary team and ensuring that all eligibility requirements are satisfied can take considerable time. Prospective applicants should therefore begin preparing early. A strong application should clearly demonstrate: 1. A relevant school leadership problem The research should address a meaningful challenge relating to school leadership in an African education context. Applicants should clearly explain the problem being investigated and why it matters. 2. A clear action-research methodology The proposal should demonstrate how the research will use an action-oriented approach and how the findings can contribute to improvements in practice. 3. Meaningful stakeholder collaboration Applicants should demonstrate how policymakers, practitioners, school leaders and/or implementing institutions will meaningfully participate in the research. 4. A qualified research team The proposed team should consist of three to five multidisciplinary members , with the Principal Investigator meeting the specified doctoral qualification and five-year requirement. 5. Practical relevance Applicants should clearly explain how the research can contribute to: Education policy School leadership practice Learning outcomes Education systems National education priorities Continental education priorities 6. Inclusion and diversity Where relevant, applicants should consider integrating issues such as: Gender equality Disability inclusion Rural education Underserved communities Marginalised groups 7. Appropriate research scope Applicants should select the grant category that corresponds to the scope of their research. A project conducted in one educational context over 12 months would align with the descriptive research category, while a study covering two or more educational contexts over 24 months would align with the comparative research category. Strong school leaders can contribute to better management, stronger teaching environments, improved organisational performance and better outcomes for learners. However, education systems across Africa face different leadership challenges depending on their national, regional and local contexts. Research that identifies these challenges and generates practical evidence can help policymakers and practitioners make better-informed decisions. The ACSL grants therefore provide an opportunity for African researchers to contribute directly to the evidence base surrounding school leadership while receiving financial support for conducting their studies. The programme s emphasis on collaboration is particularly important because research findings are more likely to have practical value when researchers work directly with the people responsible for implementing education policies and leading schools. Conclusion The African Centre for School Leadership Cohort II School Leadership Research Grants provide a significant research funding opportunity for African education researchers interested in strengthening school leadership and improving learning outcomes across the continent. With 16 descriptive grants worth up to US$15,000 each and seven comparative grants worth up to US$35,000 each , the programme will support 23 researchers undertaking action-oriented research over periods of 12 or 24 months. The opportunity is open to eligible researchers from all African countries , but applicants must meet specific requirements. In particular, the Principal Investigator must be an African citizen based in Africa and hold a doctorate in education, educational leadership, educational management or a closely related discipline earned within the past five years. Researchers whose work addresses gender equality, disability inclusion, rural and underserved communities, marginalised groups and other important education challenges are strongly encouraged to apply. title: SSN Media Fellowship 2026-2027 for Scholars New to Media Engagement: Apply for Personalized Media Training, Mentorship, and Public Communication Support
summary: The Scholars Strategy Network (SSN) has announced applications for the 2026-2027 SSN Media Fellowship, an exclusive professional development opportunity designed to support scholars who are interested in expanding their ability to communicate research findings through media platforms. The fellowship is created specifically for SSN members who are new to media engagement and want to develop the skills needed to effectively share research with wider audiences. Through personalized mentorship, practical media workshops, and guidance from experienced public scholars and SSN national staff, selected fellows will gain valuable tools for engaging with journalists, producing impactful public scholarship, and increasing the visibility of their research. Applications for the SSN Media Fellowship 2026-2027 must be submitted by September 21, 2026. About the SSN Media Fellowship The SSN Media Fellowship is entering its fourth year and continues Scholars Strategy Network’s commitment to helping researchers become stronger public communicators. The program recognizes that important research findings often have the potential to influence public discussions, policies, and communities, but many scholars may need additional support to effectively communicate their work beyond academic audiences. This fellowship provides selected SSN members with the opportunity to receive personalized guidance from experienced scholars who have successfully engaged with media outlets and public audiences. Participants will learn how to communicate their research through different media channels, including: Television interviews Radio discussions Print media Opinion articles and op-eds Digital media platforms Social media communication The fellowship is designed to help scholars develop practical media strategies and build confidence when interacting with journalists, policymakers, and the public. Fellowship Benefits and Support Provided Selected fellows will receive a combination of mentorship, training, and individualized support throughout the 2026-2027 academic year. The program includes: 1. Personalized Mentorship From Experienced Public Scholars Each selected fellow will be paired with an experienced public scholar from the Scholars Strategy Network membership. Mentors will provide practical advice, feedback, and guidance on developing effective media engagement strategies. Mentor-mentee relationships will focus on helping fellows identify opportunities to communicate their research and strengthen their public presence. Mentorship pairs are expected to meet approximately five times during the fellowship period. 2. Media Training Workshops In addition to mentorship, fellows will participate in media workshops organized by SSN national staff. These workshops will provide training and practical knowledge on topics such as: Understanding how the media works Communicating academic research clearly to non-academic audiences Developing effective media messages Preparing for interviews Writing compelling opinion pieces Building relationships with journalists and media professionals 3. Tailored Support From SSN National Staff SSN staff will provide additional assistance throughout the fellowship, including: Reviewing and editing op-ed drafts Supporting media pitches Helping fellows identify relevant media contacts Sharing media opportunities and alerts Providing guidance on effective communication strategies This support is designed to help fellows successfully translate their research into meaningful public conversations. Important Note About Funding The SSN Media Fellowship does not provide a stipend or financial award to selected fellows. The main value of the program is the professional development, mentorship, training, and networking opportunities provided through participation. Eligibility Requirements for the SSN Media Fellowship To be considered for the fellowship, applicants must: Be current members of the Scholars Strategy Network Be interested in improving their media engagement skills Have research projects that can be communicated to public audiences Be relatively new to media work or looking to strengthen their existing media experience Be willing to participate actively in mentorship meetings and media workshops throughout the academic year Due to program limitations, applications are only accepted from current SSN members. Application Requirements Applicants must complete an online application form and provide the following information: Personal Information Applicants are required to submit: First name Last name Email address Research Project Description Applicants must provide a short description or abstract of the research project or projects that they would like to focus on during their media engagement activities. The research should be suitable for public communication and demonstrate potential value for broader audiences. Media Engagement Statement Applicants must submit a statement of between 500 and 1,000 words explaining: Their interest in media engagement Any previous media experience they have Their goals for participating in the fellowship How the fellowship will support their professional development Mentor-Mentee Meeting Interests Applicants should explain what they hope to explore during mentor meetings throughout the fellowship. This may include areas such as: Developing a media strategy Improving public communication skills Learning how to engage journalists Identifying opportunities for sharing research Receiving feedback on media-related projects Curriculum Vitae Applicants must provide a link to their most recent CV. The CV should highlight relevant academic, professional, research, and public engagement experiences. Additional Information Applicants may also share any additional information, ideas, or thoughts regarding potential mentor pairings. This section is optional but allows applicants to provide further context about their interests and goals. October 2026 Selected fellows will be notified and matched with mentors. All fellows will also participate in an onboarding session before beginning mentor meetings and media workshops. November 2026 The first media workshop led by SSN national staff will take place. Spring 2027 Fellows will participate in two additional media workshops led by SSN staff. June 2027 The fellowship program will officially conclude, followed by an evaluation of the program experience. Why Apply for the SSN Media Fellowship? The SSN Media Fellowship offers scholars an opportunity to move beyond traditional academic communication and connect their research with communities, decision-makers, and the wider public. By participating in this program, fellows can develop stronger communication skills, gain confidence in media engagement, receive personalized advice from experienced scholars, and learn strategies for making research more accessible and impactful. For researchers interested in increasing the reach and influence of their work, the fellowship provides a valuable platform for developing public scholarship skills. How to Apply Interested applicants should complete the official application form before the deadline. Apply HERE Applicants with questions may contact Dominik Doemer, Director of Communications at Scholars Strategy Network, through dominik@scholars.org. Conclusion The SSN Media Fellowship 2026-2027 is a valuable opportunity for Scholars Strategy Network members who want to strengthen their ability to communicate research through media and public platforms. Through expert mentorship, practical workshops, and personalized support, selected fellows will gain the knowledge and confidence needed to share important research findings with broader audiences. Eligible SSN members interested in developing their media engagement skills and expanding the public impact of their research are encouraged to submit their applications before the September 21, 2026 deadline. title: Safe Arborist Techniques Fund Grant Program 2026: Up to $15,000 Research Funding for Tree Safety, Arborist Innovation, Climbing Techniques, Rigging Systems, and Safer Tree Care Practices
summary: The Safe Arborist Techniques Fund (SATF) Grant Program 2026 is an important research funding opportunity supporting innovation, safety improvement, and knowledge development within the arboriculture and tree care industry. The program is jointly established by the Tree Research and Education Endowment Fund (TREE Fund) and the International Society of Arboriculture (ISA) to support research and development focused on improving the techniques, equipment, and safety practices used by arborists when climbing, rigging, and working with trees. Through this grant program, researchers and institutions are encouraged to develop evidence-based solutions that help create safer working environments for arborists while improving understanding of tree work risks, equipment performance, and hazard identification. The SATF Grant Program provides funding of up to $15,000 per project and expects funded projects to be completed within two years from the initial fund disbursement . About the Safe Arborist Techniques Fund (SATF) The tree care profession involves complex and physically demanding activities, including tree climbing, equipment operation, rigging, and managing hazardous situations. Arborists often work in environments where safety risks can arise from: Tree structure and stability Equipment limitations Rigging techniques Climbing methods Environmental conditions Human factors during tree operations The Safe Arborist Techniques Fund was created to support research that addresses these challenges and develops practical solutions that protect arborists and improve industry standards. The program focuses on advancing: Safer climbing techniques Improved rigging practices Better arborist equipment Hazard identification methods Workplace safety systems Evidence-based tree care practices Grant Benefits Successful applicants may receive: Research funding of up to $15,000 Support for innovative arboriculture safety research Opportunity to contribute to improved industry standards Platform to share findings with researchers and tree care professionals Opportunity to publish research outcomes in professional journals Recognition through TREE Fund research networks Funded researchers are expected to contribute knowledge that can benefit arborists, urban forestry professionals, researchers, and organizations involved in tree management. Areas of Research Supported TREE Fund welcomes research proposals from a broad range of academic and technical disciplines. Projects may involve: Qualitative research Quantitative research Engineering studies Safety assessments Equipment and technique evaluation Risk identification studies Arboriculture technology development Research should contribute to improving safety in areas such as: Tree climbing Rigging operations Arborist equipment Tree work procedures Hazard prevention Projects Not Eligible for Funding The SATF Grant Program does not support certain types of projects. Applications will not be accepted for: 1. Individual Grants The program does not provide grants directly to individuals. Funding must be connected to eligible research institutions or organizations. 2. Municipal Tree Surveys or Assessments Projects primarily focused on municipal tree inventories, surveys, or assessments are not eligible. 3. Tree Planting Programs Funding is not available for tree planting initiatives. 4. Traditional Forestry and Conservation Studies Projects focused mainly on: Forestry production Timber management Agroforestry Forest ecology Conservation of natural forests are not eligible. 5. Product Testing for Commercial Benefit Research focused primarily on testing a product for the benefit of the company manufacturing that product will not be funded. Application Timeline and Important Deadlines The SATF Grant application process follows a structured timeline. Letter of Intent (LOI) Period Opening Date: August 1, 2026 LOI Submission Deadline: September 1, 2026 TREE Fund will only accept Letters of Intent between August 1 and September 1, 2026. Proposal Review Notification September 15, 2026 Applicants whose Letters of Intent meet the requirements will be invited to submit a full proposal. Full Proposal Submission Deadline October 15, 2026 Only applicants whose LOIs are approved will be allowed to submit complete applications. Grant Recipient Notification Mid-to-late December 2026 Selected applicants will be informed of funding decisions. Application Process The application process consists of two major stages: Step 1: Submit a Letter of Intent (LOI) Applicants must first submit an LOI through the online application portal. The Letter of Intent must clearly identify: Principal Investigator (PI) Institution responsible for conducting the research Research concept Alignment with SATF priorities TREE Fund reviews each LOI to determine whether: The project meets eligibility requirements The research aligns with program goals The project has reasonable potential for success Only approved LOIs move forward to the full application stage. Step 2: Submit Full Research Proposal Applicants invited after LOI approval must submit a complete proposal by: October 15, 2026 The full proposal must provide detailed information about the research project, methodology, budget, and expected outcomes. Application Requirements Applicants must provide information about: Principal Investigator Co-Principal Investigators Student assistants (if applicable) Curriculum vitae information The proposal must include the following sections: 1. Project Description Overall Project Summary (Maximum 400 words) Applicants must explain: The current problem being addressed The impact of the issue on arboriculture and urban forestry The goals of the proposed research 2. Measurable Outputs and Outcomes (Maximum 250 words) Applicants should describe: Expected research outputs Publications Educational materials Presentations Outreach activities Applicants should also identify up to five measurable outcomes showing how the research may improve tree care practices. 3. Current Knowledge and Previous Research (Maximum 1,000 words) This section should include: Existing knowledge about the research topic Previous attempts to address the problem Relevant scientific literature Experience of the research team 4. Project Work Plan (Maximum 1,500 words) Applicants must clearly explain: Research scope Research objectives Hypotheses Study design Methodology Data analysis approach Any commercial or proprietary elements 5. Dissemination Plan (Maximum 300 words) Applicants should explain how research findings will be shared with: Academic communities Arboriculture professionals Industry stakeholders TREE Fund encourages researchers to make findings widely available. 6. Literature References Applicants should provide relevant citations following recognized academic citation standards. Budget Requirements Applicants must provide detailed budget information, including: Eligible Budget Categories Institutional compensation Research stipends Employee benefits Travel expenses Transportation costs Equipment purchases Materials and supplies Contract labor Consultants Speakers Institutional overhead Other expenses Institutional overhead is limited to: Maximum 10% Applicants must also identify: Cash contributions from other sources In-kind support A minimum of: 10% additional funding support is required. Selection Criteria Applications are reviewed based on several important factors. TREE Fund reviewers will focus on: 1. Research Team Experience Reviewers consider: Previous achievements Research experience Expertise of investigators Early-career researchers are encouraged to collaborate with experienced researchers or advisors. 2. Contribution to Arboriculture Projects should demonstrate clear potential to improve: Arborist safety Tree care practices Industry knowledge 3. Research Approach Evaluation includes: Strength of research questions Experimental design Methodology Scientific quality 4. Dissemination Strategy Reviewers assess how effectively findings will reach: Researchers Tree care professionals Industry stakeholders Diversity and Inclusion Statement TREE Fund does not discriminate based on: Race Color Creed Gender Sexual orientation Disability National origin Ethnic background The organization welcomes applications from diverse researchers and institutions. However, current TREE Fund trustees and immediate family members of trustees are not eligible to receive grants. Award Process and Fund Distribution Grant recommendations are reviewed by the TREE Fund Research and Education Committee before being presented to the TREE Fund Board of Trustees. Grant approvals occur during: Spring Grants: May Board Meeting Fall Grants: December Board Meeting Recipients receive written notification within one month of trustee approval. Successful applicants must complete: Grant agreement forms Payment schedules Reporting requirements Required documentation Reporting Requirements TREE Fund expects research findings to be shared widely so they can benefit the arboriculture community. Grant recipients should: Notify TREE Fund when research findings are published Inform TREE Fund about conference presentations Acknowledge TREE Fund support in publications and presentations Share title: Erasmus Mundus Scholarships 2027 | Fully Funded Master’s Scholarships in Europe for International Students
summary: Applications for the prestigious Erasmus Mundus Joint Masters Scholarships 2027 are expected to open soon for international students worldwide. Funded by the European Union , these fully funded scholarships provide an opportunity to pursue a high-quality international master s degree while studying at multiple universities across Europe and beyond. Erasmus Mundus Joint Masters are among Europe s most prestigious international master s programmes. They are jointly designed and delivered by a consortium of leading universities from different countries, offering students a unique international learning experience, world-class education, and global career opportunities. Outstanding applicants may receive fully funded scholarships covering tuition, living expenses, travel, and visa costs. Unlike traditional master s programmes, Erasmus Mundus students typically study in at least two countries during their degree and graduate with either a joint degree or multiple degrees awarded by the participating universities. Whether you are interested in engineering, public health, climate change, data science, international development, business, law, artificial intelligence, or social sciences, the Erasmus Mundus Catalogue features hundreds of internationally recognised master s programmes taught in English. Funded by the European Union , these fully funded scholarships allow outstanding students to pursue a joint master s degree at some of Europe s top universities while studying in multiple countries. The Erasmus Mundus Joint Masters (EMJM) programme is one of the world s most competitive international scholarship programmes, offering students a unique opportunity to earn a joint or multiple master s degrees through an integrated study programme delivered by a consortium of universities across Europe and beyond. Whether you re looking to advance your academic career, gain international experience, or build a global professional network, the Erasmus Mundus Scholarship is an excellent opportunity to study abroad with full financial support. Why Apply for Erasmus Mundus Scholarships? The Erasmus Mundus Joint Masters programme offers students the opportunity to: Study at multiple universities in different countries. Gain international academic and cultural experience. Receive a joint or multiple master s degree recognized worldwide. Learn from leading academics and industry experts. Participate in research projects, internships, traineeships, and thesis work depending on the programme. Build a strong international professional network. Programmes are jointly designed and delivered by at least three higher education institutions from three different countries , together with academic and industry partners. Erasmus Mundus Scholarship Benefits Outstanding applicants may receive a fully funded scholarship covering: Full participation or tuition costs Monthly living allowance Travel expenses Visa costs Installation and other eligible programme-related support Scholarship benefits are awarded directly by the selected Erasmus Mundus programme and may vary slightly depending on the consortium. Programme Duration Erasmus Mundus Joint Masters typically last: 1 year (60 ECTS) 1.5 years (90 ECTS) 2 years (120 ECTS) Students study at different partner universities throughout the programme and graduate with either: A Joint Master s Degree , or Multiple Master s Degrees issued by participating universities. Who Can Apply? Students from all countries worldwide are eligible to apply. Applicants must: Hold a bachelor s degree (or equivalent), or Be in their final year of undergraduate studies and graduate before the master s programme begins. Some programmes may have additional academic or language requirements depending on the field of study. Required Documents Application requirements vary by programme, but commonly include: Bachelor s degree certificate (or proof of final-year enrolment) Academic transcripts Curriculum Vitae (CV) Letter of Motivation or Statement of Purpose Letters of Recommendation Proof of English language proficiency (where required) Passport or national identification document Some programmes may also request: Research proposal Portfolio Relevant work experience Additional programme-specific documents Always check the official website of your chosen programme for the complete list of requirements. How to Apply for Erasmus Mundus Scholarships 2027 Unlike many scholarship programmes, there is no central Erasmus Mundus application portal . To apply: Visit the official Erasmus Mundus Catalogue. Search for programmes that match your academic background and interests. Visit the official website of your selected programme. Carefully review the admission requirements and scholarship criteria. Submit your application directly to the consortium running the programme before its deadline. Applicants should also contact the programme coordinators if they have questions regarding admissions or scholarship availability. When to Apply Most Erasmus Mundus Joint Master s programmes accept applications between October and January for programmes beginning the following academic year. Application deadlines differ for each programme, so applicants should regularly check the official programme website. Tips for a Strong Erasmus Mundus Application To improve your chances of receiving a scholarship: Maintain a strong academic record. Write a compelling and personalized motivation letter. Obtain high-quality recommendation letters. Highlight leadership, volunteer work, research, internships, and extracurricular achievements. Demonstrate how the programme aligns with your academic and career goals. Apply early and ensure all required documents are submitted before the deadline. Erasmus Mundus Scholarships in Numbers Since its launch, almost 50,000 students from around the world have participated in Erasmus Mundus programmes, making it one of Europe s most successful international scholarship initiatives. Application Deadline Varies by programme. Most scholarship applications close between October and January , although exact dates depend on each master s programme. title: ACLS Digital Justice Grants 2026-27 | Up to $100,000 for Digital Scholarship Projects
summary: Applications are now open for the 2026-27 ACLS Digital Justice Grants Program , a funding opportunity designed to support innovative digital projects across the humanities and social sciences. Administered by the American Council of Learned Societies (ACLS) and generously funded by the Mellon Foundation, the program seeks to advance equitable and inclusive digital scholarship that critically engages with the histories, experiences, and interests of historically marginalized communities. The program offers both Seed Grants and Development Grants to scholars and research teams using ethical digital methods to expand access to knowledge, strengthen community engagement, and promote justice-centered approaches to digital humanities and social science research. About the ACLS Digital Justice Grants Program The ACLS Digital Justice Grants Program aims to address long-standing inequities in access to digital tools, resources, and institutional support within the humanities and interpretive social sciences. The initiative supports projects that center the experiences of historically marginalized communities, including but not limited to: * Black communities * Latinx communities * Indigenous communities * People with disabilities * Queer, trans, and gender nonconforming communities * Other historically underrepresented groups By funding innovative digital scholarship, ACLS seeks to promote inclusion, sustainability, and broader participation in the digital transformation of humanistic inquiry. Grant Categories Digital Justice Seed Grants Seed Grants are designed for projects in the early stages of development. Funding Amount : $10,000 – $25,000 These grants support: * Planning workshops * Prototype development * Testing new methodologies * Exploring innovative research agendas * Experimenting with new source materials and digital approaches Digital Justice Development Grants Development Grants support projects that have moved beyond the proof-of-concept stage and are ready for expansion. Funding Amount :$50,000 – $100,000 These grants support projects that: * Demonstrate significant preliminary work * Have evidence of scholarly or public engagement * Require resources for the next stage of development * Have clear plans for technological, intellectual, and financial sustainability What Types of Projects Are Supported ? The program supports projects that use digital tools and methods to advance justice-oriented scholarship and community engagement. Eligible activities include: * Ethical digital projects focused on historically marginalized communities * Capacity-building initiatives in digital humanities * Publicly engaged projects developed with community partners * Pedagogical initiatives that train students in digital humanities methods * Collaborative projects connecting scholars across institutions * Projects that develop new technological infrastructure for research and public engagement * Digital knowledge dissemination and content-building initiatives Additional Support for Grant Recipients In addition to grant funding, all recipients will have access to financial planning coaching provided by the Nonprofit Finance Fund. This support helps projects develop long-term sustainability strategies and stewardship plans beyond the grant period. Eligibility Criteria To apply, projects must meet the following requirements: * The Principal Investigator must be a scholar in the humanities or interpretive social sciences. * Awarded funds must be administered by a U.S. institution of higher education. * Projects should be made as openly accessible as intellectual property considerations allow. * Seed Grant applicants must be in the start-up or prototyping phase. * Development Grant applicants must demonstrate substantial prior work and public or scholarly impact. Ineligible Projects ACLS Digital Justice Grants do not support projects whose sole or primary focus is: * Creative works such as novels or films * Textbooks * Straightforward translations * Purely pedagogical projects Institutional indirect costs are also not covered under this funding opportunity.
